reasons: The rule is protective of the Customer (limiting audits of our usage); the document contains no audit, inspection, records-examination or system-access right binding the Customer, so the absence is more favorable than the preferred position and correctly recorded as compliant rather than 'missing' (a 'missing' finding would perversely invite a Vendor audit right).

Cited paragraphs support the rationale: p0001's access/cooperation language is operational delivery support, not an audit or remote-system-access right; p0023 (fees) and p0025 (use covenants) create no verification mechanic.
Consistent with the claimed compliant status, no redline was rendered (redline text is identical to originals) and no counterparty comment was proposed, as expected.
The failed deterministic 'audit frequency limited' check is non-probative here because there is no audit clause for the pattern to match; the rationale accurately explains this.
